easy.def: Work that a person does to earn money.
examples: Dad has a new job.
She likes her job.
A baker has a job.

more.def: The work that a person does regularly to earn money.
examples: My aunt has a job at the post office.
A firefighter has an important job in our town.
He is looking for a job after school.

easy.def: A task you have to do.
examples: Feeding the fish is my job.
It was a big job.
She did a good job.

more.def: A task or duty that someone has to do.
examples: Setting the table is my job on school nights.
Cleaning the garage was a big job.
You did a great job on your science poster.
The jockey rode the horse.
A jockey is small.
The jockey wore bright colors.

more.def: A person whose job is to ride horses in races.
examples: The jockey leaned low over the horse.
The jockey wore a bright cap and silks.
A small jockey won the race.
Join the two pieces.
The bridge joins two towns.
Join hands in a circle.

more.def: To connect or fasten things together.
examples: A bridge joins the two sides of the river.
Join the two ropes with a knot.
The two streams join to make one river.

easy.def: To become part of a group.
examples: Join our team.
She joined the club.
Can I join you?

more.def: To become a member of a group, or to do something together with others.
examples: She joined the choir last fall.
Can I join you for lunch?
Several new players joined the team.

easy.def: A place where two bones meet.
examples: My knee is a joint.
Joints let you bend.
The elbow is a joint.

more.def: A place in the body where two bones meet and can move.
examples: Your knee is a joint.
Joints let your arms and legs bend.
The doctor checked her elbow joint.

easy.def: A place where two things are joined.
examples: The joint in the pipe.
The wood joint is tight.
A joint in the table.

more.def: A place where two parts are joined together.
examples: Glue held the joint of the chair.
The plumber fixed a leaking joint in the pipe.
The two boards meet at a tight joint.

easy.def: Something funny you say to make people laugh.
examples: Tell us a joke.
Her joke was funny.
I know a joke about a cow.

more.def: A funny story or saying that makes people laugh.
examples: My dad tells a joke at every dinner.
The clown's joke made the whole class laugh.
She told a joke about a talking banana.
I was only joking.
He jokes with us.
They joked at lunch.

more.def: To say something funny or not serious, to make people laugh.
examples: Dad joked that the dog was reading the paper.
She was only joking when she said she would eat the whole cake.
The friends joked and laughed all through lunch.
My dad is a joker.
The joker made us laugh.
He is a class joker.

more.def: A person who likes to tell jokes and play tricks.
examples: My dad is a joker who loves puns.
The class joker made us all laugh.
The joker wore a funny hat.

easy.def: A playing card with a picture of a clown.
examples: I got the joker.
The joker is in the deck.
The joker is a card.

more.def: A card in a deck with a picture of a jester, used in some games.
examples: I drew the joker from the deck.
The joker is a wild card.
The deck has two jokers.
The jolly man laughed a lot.
The jolly baker sang as he worked.
We sang a jolly song.

more.def: Cheerful, friendly, and full of good humor.
examples: Our jolly uncle always tells the funniest jokes.
The jolly crowd sang songs on the bus ride home.
Grandpa was in a jolly mood at the party.

easy.def: A book where you write what happens each day.
examples: I write in my journal.
The journal is blue.
She keeps a journal.

more.def: A notebook in which you write about your thoughts and what you do each day.
examples: I write in my journal every night.
The explorer kept a journal of his trip.
She read her old journal.
The journalist wrote a story.
A journalist asked a question.
The journalist works at a paper.

more.def: A person whose job is to gather and write news for newspapers, TV or the internet.
examples: The journalist wrote a story about the flood.
A journalist asked the mayor a question.
The journalist reported live from the scene.
The journey to Grandma's house takes all day.
The bird's journey is very long.
We packed food for the journey.

more.def: A trip from one place to another, usually a long one.
examples: The explorers began their journey across the frozen land.
The journey by train took two days.
Salmon make a long journey up the river.
The puppy jumped with joy.
We sang with joy.
The baby's laugh brings me joy.
Her face was full of joy when she saw her grandparents.
The team jumped for joy when they won.
Reading is one of the great joys of my life.
